stem:
A 28-year-old man arrives in hemorrhagic shock after a motor vehicle collision. There is no time to type and cross-match his blood before transfusion.

Which of the following donor blood types is most appropriate for this emergency transfusion?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None; O-negative cells carry neither A, B, nor Rh(D) antigens.
options.explanation: In emergencies without time for cross-matching, blood from a universal donor — an individual with type O negative blood — may be transfused because its cells lack the antigens that trigger recipient antibody attack.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Absence of one antigen set is being mistaken for absence of all.
options.explanation: Type A cells carry A antigens, which recipient anti-A antibodies (present in type B and type O patients) would agglutinate; only O-negative lacks both A and B antigens.

options.label: C
options.misconception: The universal-recipient type is being confused with the universal-donor type.
options.explanation: AB-positive blood carries A, B, and Rh(D) antigens on its cells and would be attacked by antibodies in most recipients; AB individuals are universal recipients, not donors.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Rh negativity alone is being treated as universal compatibility.
options.explanation: Type B cells carry B antigens and would be agglutinated by anti-B antibodies in type A and type O recipients; Rh status is not the only compatibility issue.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Dropping the Rh antigen is being treated as sufficient for universality.
options.explanation: AB-negative cells still carry both A and B antigens, so recipients with either anti-A or anti-B antibodies would hemolyze them; only type O lacks both.

context: Learning objective: choose emergency transfusion blood. Blood groups reflect antigen markers on erythrocyte membranes; recipient antibodies attack mismatched antigens. Type O-negative cells carry neither A nor B nor Rh(D) antigens, making O-negative the universal donor for uncrossmatched transfusion.
